note: 2026-10-16: two R-modes. Scanned the 250-trace tracework split of the Oct-13 dump; 103 non-coding sessions were reviewed on 2026-10-16 (b9 nc-batch-0..4: 58 failure modes, 25 marked new, 33 already mapped to T/L/D modes by the reviewers). Each of the 25 new modes and the 10 candidate slips named for curation was checked against the library and, where it was decisive, against the session text. R1 (additive layer read as an override; one strong session, one weak) and R2 (planned quantity over a capacity fixed by other parties' facts; two sessions) qualify. Every other candidate is covered by a T/L/D mode, rests on a stated instruction or open-world knowledge, is conversational, or was not a slip on inspection; the 2026-10-16 entries in 'considered' say which. 2026-10-15 (kept): tools/trace_traps.py scanned the 281 unused non-coding sessions of the Oct-13 dump and admitted none; its four rejected patterns are the first entries in 'considered' (research/TRACE-signal-yield.md gives the detail). The 'considered' key is documentation only; traplib.py reads schema, source, generated and modes.

considered.pattern: scope bleed: the assistant edits or adds beyond the authorised scope, and the user says it was not asked for

traces.signal: User authorised spelling fixes only; the assistant reworded sentences and added explanations, then conceded.
Kitchen render gained an appliance the user never asked for; the reference photo showed another type.
Garment views: only the front view was right; other views altered a detail outside the requested change.

considered.verdict: rejected: 3 sessions in total, 2 of them image edits. The authorisation is a stated instruction (dead), and the over-application mechanism is already T9 (rule-scope shield) and L12 (a by-design irregularity 'fixed').

considered.pattern: a reference or official source supplied by the user overrides the assistant's figure or default

traces.signal: User points to the officially published iteration figure, which differs from the one the assistant used.
User supplies the governing policy text, with an older and a newer name by year, before the answer.
User says two reference files contradict the prompt, and names which reference governs one item.

considered.verdict: rejected: covered by T6 (which source or edition governs, by date) and L2/L9. TRAP-CATALOG-B7 s6 also lists context-versus-memory conflicts as solved by current models.

considered.pattern: the user corrects a figure the assistant computed from a count or split

traces.signal: User says a timed video splits into fewer fixed-length scenes than the assistant counted.
User says the rounding of percentage splits applied to a daily volume is wrong and supplies figures.
User questions whether a lift used one weight or a pair, which halves the computed load.

considered.verdict: rejected: covered by T2 (convention from worked figures) and T3 (quantity basis, per piece versus per pair).

considered.pattern: the user corrects their own earlier premise, or forwards a later fact, mid-session

traces.signal: User retracts their own earlier justification for an equipment purchase and restates the real basis.
User finds evidence that a model the assistant ruled unavailable is sold locally; the assistant reverses.
User relays new information about the learner's prior knowledge after the lesson plan was built.

considered.verdict: rejected: covered by L9 (the request presupposes a fact the records refute), L1 (later restatement) and T8 (changed premise, filler only).

considered.pattern: a headline discount or cashback applied to a product line its terms do not cover

traces.signal: A large headline cashback was applied to a consumer line; the terms limited it to workstation lines, capped lower.

considered.verdict: covered by T9 (a real rule on a neighbouring item over-applied); the inferred line-membership form is D11 (dead).

considered.pattern: a bundled component's upstream fix version entered as the product's fix version

traces.signal: Vulnerability register mixed product and bundled-library advisories; the assistant kept library versions apart from product releases.

considered.verdict: covered by L7 (a component figure taken for the whole). No slip observed: the session's assistant separated the command-line-only advisory and mapped the library fix to a product release.

considered.pattern: a generic adjustment rule overrides the item-specific label rate

traces.signal: Assistant doubled the seed rate by a generic silage rule; the user insisted on the bag-label rate.

considered.verdict: covered by T3 (the label rate is already on the use's basis, cued on the record) with T9 as the shield; the generic rule came from the assistant's memory, not from a document.

considered.pattern: an illustrative worked total taken as a binding legal limit

traces.signal: An annual overtime total computed only to show scale was treated as a statutory ceiling; the assistant corrected the user.

considered.verdict: rejected: the user's slip, caught by the assistant. The fixture form is D3 (stored figure vs derivation; dead) or T9 (a figure for a neighbouring case over-applied).

considered.pattern: an optional cost booked as mandatory

traces.signal: Assistant listed buying standards documents as a required cost; the user disputed it and free legal sources existed.

considered.verdict: covered by T4 (an item listed as needed is already available) and L9; the trace slip rests on open-world legal knowledge, not on records.

considered.pattern: a record-level override field let win over the base definition of the field

traces.signal: Assistant let a step-level override field win; the user said the level comes only from the area definition.

considered.verdict: covered by T9: a real instance-over-template rule for other fields over-applied to a field defined from the area level. The cumulative-layers slip in the same session became R1.

considered.pattern: a verdict flipped when the candidate set was narrowed

traces.signal: The assistant's ore-deposit match changed when the user cut the list to two; the evidence was unchanged.

considered.verdict: rejected: conversational instability, not a reading of records; the fixture form (scores re-normalised over a narrowed field) is L12.

considered.pattern: an estimate range straddling a threshold counted as clearing it

traces.signal: A lot whose estimated net range dipped below the required profit was listed as passing (review finding).

considered.verdict: covered by T2 (which end of a range, fixed by worked figures); not confirmable in the truncated transcript.

considered.pattern: the principal's own wording taken over the records (a later request against their own ban, a complaint label against the evidence, a gloss against the source term)

Complaint classified by the user's words as a format defect; the attached screenshot showed a missing file.
User's English gloss for an evidence type was read literally; the source-language term meant any written report.

considered.verdict: covered by L9 (the request presupposes a fact the records refute); cd09's inferred class-membership form is D11 (dead) and its re-check form D14 (dead).

considered.pattern: a name token read as the item's generation, grade or genuineness

traces.signal: A chip named like the new tier but on the older architecture was recommended as current generation.
Reviewer suspected a cheap professional-model listing was priced at genuine resale; the assistant had labelled it a copy.

considered.verdict: covered by D4 (near-twin names; dead): d00f's miss was a near-twin series-name token. A title that misstates the model is T1/T5; c632 shows no slip.

considered.pattern: a narrowed requirement silently reverting in the final deliverable

traces.signal: An agreed high-performance processor series reverted to the low-power series in the final shortlist.

considered.verdict: covered by T8 (filler) and D14 (changed premise as a decisive trap; dead).

considered.pattern: a run condition set before a component was added, above that component's boiling point

traces.signal: Two runs were set at a temperature above two co-solvents' boiling points; flagged only when safety was asked.

considered.verdict: rejected: the runs used sealed reactors, where solvothermal work above a co-solvent's boiling point is routine; a limit that holds for one vessel type is T9, and the re-check form is D14 (dead).

considered.pattern: absence, private inputs or missing pages filled in by the assistant

traces.signal: Concluded a variant was not sold locally after finding only foreign part numbers.
Filled a client's recipe quantities and ingredient costs with typical values only the client holds.
Wrote lessons for a truncated chapter's missing sections from its topic list.

considered.verdict: covered by D6 and D10 (dead): determinability and gap filling.

considered.pattern: rank and frame checks in a claim audit

traces.signal: Supplied post-mortem: a ranking claim was checked only against the named clubs; an unnamed row changed the rank.

considered.verdict: rejected: a population or coverage check (D7, D11; dead) or subjective frame wording; the post-mortem rows were a human team's errors.

traces.signal: Template's function column taken as formula text to display instead of working functions.
Discovery questions written assuming the patient profile they exist to discover.
A descriptive formula was tested on physical spaces when the user meant their photographs.

modes.name: Additive local layer read as an override of the base schedule
modes.summary: Default: when a base schedule and a same-named local layer (a site, region, package or project file with the same title, columns and item names) both carry an entry for one item, the agent keeps one entry, usually letting the later or more specific layer override the base, and drops the other. The files make that wrong because the layers add: a governing entitlement from another party guarantees the base entry to everyone in scope, so the override reading breaches it, and a different party's worked line items show both elements paid together; nothing says how the layers combine. Trace support is essentially ONE session (01a0ce05: the user corrected that same-named files across packages are cumulative after the assistant had let the later package's duplicates win); 01a0d332 is weaker support (a security verdict that turned on how a project-level file combines with global settings, and the first pass dropped that layer). aimed_at both is an expectation, not a measurement: Fable's newest/most-specific default and Astra's silent keyed join (last write wins) both keep one layer. Not measured here; pilot first.

recipe.record: A local-layer schedule with the same title, columns and item names as the base schedule, later dated and more specific (site, region, package or project), carrying an entry for the item the deliverable prices; read alone it looks like a complete restatement of the base.
recipe.anchors: (1) A governing document of another party (collective agreement, master contract, group policy) guarantees the base entry to everyone in scope, so reading the local entry as a replacement breaches it for the affected item. (2) A different party's worked line items for one comparable case (payroll bureau payslip extract, carrier invoice, insurer's premium breakdown) show the base and local elements as two lines. (3) Optional: the local owner's budget note costs only the local element, named by description, never by a figure a script can match.
recipe.withheld: No 'in addition', 'top-up', 'supplement', 'replaces' or 'supersedes' wording in any title, header or note; no sentence on how layers combine; the mechanism (a local element paid on top of the base) is supplied by the model.
dials: the entitlement anchor is the strong notch: pilot with it and the worked line items only
for Astra change the kind of evidence (a cost-centre ledger split) rather than adding another remark
a local entry smaller than the guaranteed base makes override impossible; a larger one only makes it implausible: choose deliberately and record which
keep the affected population small: one to three items that appear in both layers
recipe.conservation: Grade the per-item total and its split by payer or cost centre (base vs local), so keeping one layer, booking the sum under one payer, or counting the local entry twice each misses.
recipe.shields: A real precedence rule scoped to a neighbouring item (site schedules replace group rates for overtime, say); Fable may cite it, and the audit must show its grammar does not reach the trapped item.

proof_obligations: uniqueness: only base plus local satisfies every anchor; override, base-only and double counting each break one
consistency: every item present in both layers combines the same way; no overlapping item supports the override reading
ablation: dropping the entitlement anchor leaves the worked line items deciding; dropping both leaves the item undecided, and the validator reports it
executed counterfactual: the override reading produces a different deliverable on every check routed through the item
census of wrong answers: override, base-only, sum under one payer and local counted twice each fail at least one graded check
no anomaly under the default: the override reading leaves no unmatched row or missing value
blind reader reaches the additive reading with no sentence stating how layers combine
hazards: Real layering conventions differ (configuration files override; tariffs and allowances often add): built on file structure alone the item is ambiguous, so the entitlement or worked-line anchor is mandatory
With a worked figure as the only anchor this is T7 (a convention from two parties' worked figures), not R1
Inverse of L11 (one event under two document numbers counted twice): never route both through one pair of schedules in a task
Base-only items must still price under the override default, or the gap is an anomaly the agent's own script finds
01a0ce05 is a data-extraction session rejected as requires_execution: the mechanism transfers, the fixture must be a written schedule a reader can check
kills: a title, header or note calling the local file a supplement, top-up or replacement (a stated rule, D1)
a sentence saying local entries are paid in addition to, or instead of, base entries
a worked line labelled with the local file's name beside the trapped item
trace_signals: the user says same-named files or schedules across packages, sites or versions are cumulative, not alternatives
the assistant resolved duplicate entries by letting the later or more specific source win
a verdict depends on how a project-level or local file combines with global settings
domains: written reviews of layered policy or configuration settings
modes.example: A group allowance schedule and a site schedule both list a remote-shift meal allowance per grade under the same name. The collective agreement guarantees the group allowance to all staff, and the payroll bureau's payslip extract for another site worker shows two meal lines. Deliverable: a per-worker monthly allowance register with the group and site cost-centre totals.

traces.signal: User corrected that same-named files across packages add together; the assistant had let later packages' duplicates win.
Security verdict turned on a repository config file overriding global permission settings; the first pass ignored that layer.

modes.name: Planned quantity exceeds a capacity fixed only by other parties' facts
modes.summary: Default: the agent derives a plan quantity top-down from the principal's driver (leads times conversion rates, a compressed timeline, a target volume) and carries it into the schedule without checking the supply side. The files make that wrong because routine documents from two other parties (a clinician's rota and the receptionist's slot length; a teaching timetable and the field plan's visit lengths) fix a capacity the plan cannot exceed; no document states the capacity as a number or says the target is infeasible. Seen in TWO sessions: 01a0c97e (monthly evaluation targets one professional could not see) and 01a0d157 (a one-year fieldwork plan infeasible for teaching lecturers); both assistants conceded once the user objected. Kin to L9 (the work order presupposes a feasible target) and D3 (stored figure vs derivation, dead): stating the capacity turns it into D3. aimed_at both is an expectation: Astra applies the top-down default silently, Fable tends to add a caveat and keep the target (01a0c97e's assistant said its caveat came after the numbers). Not measured here; pilot first.

recipe.record: The principal's plan or KPI sheet (a dated folder document, never the task instruction) states the target volume or schedule, derived top-down and internally consistent; the deliverable carries it into a dated plan.
recipe.anchors: (1) A second party's routine operating document fixes the supply side by structure, not by a capacity figure (a rota listing the sessions the clinician holds for evaluations; a timetable showing teaching weeks). (2) A third party's routine record fixes what each item consumes, by description (the receptionist's handbook: one evaluation fills one session slot of a stated length; the field plan: each site visit takes a stated span of days). (3) Optional notch: a by-the-way remark that the sessions are already full, or that teaching blocks travel.
recipe.withheld: No sentence states the capacity as a number, says the target exceeds it, or ranks the target against the rota; the governing text states only the positive general rule (evaluations are booked into the clinician's evaluation sessions; fieldwork happens outside teaching weeks).
dials: each extra witness of the limit (a full diary export, a cancelled-visit note) is one notch toward solvable
printing the capacity as a figure anywhere is a large notch and turns the premise into D3 (dead)
for Astra change the kind of evidence (a booking export) rather than adding a remark
keep the capped population small: one or two weeks or phases where the plan exceeds the limit
recipe.conservation: Grade the capped quantity and a downstream figure only the capped plan reconciles (leads to contact, attendances expected, travel budget), so booking the target with a caveat, or capping without carrying it downstream, misses.
recipe.shields: A real growth or minimum-volume rule scoped to another quantity (a marketing lead-volume commitment, a funder's minimum output count), which Fable may cite to keep the target.

proof_obligations: uniqueness: the anchors fix exactly one capacity under every reading of the rota and slot length, and the target lies outside it by a wide margin
ablation: dropping either structural anchor leaves the capacity undetermined; the validator shows both are needed
executed counterfactual: the uncapped plan yields a different deliverable on every check routed through the cap
census of wrong answers: the target, the target with a caveat, a cap from one anchor, and the cap without downstream changes each fail a graded check
no anomaly under the default: the uncapped plan leaves no overbooked slot, unmatched row or stated total in the deliverable
blind reader caps the plan with no sentence that states the capacity
hazards: If the task's principal binds the target ('book the KPI') and nothing makes the supply-side rule govern, a blind reader keeps the target: unfair. The booking rule must be a real, positive SOP sentence
If the deliverable assigns individual slots or dates, the default overbooks visibly and the agent's own check finds it; grade weekly or phase totals
A limit known only from general knowledge (boiling points, statutory hours) must be supplied by a party in the folder; otherwise the rule has a missing input (an audit-rejected shape)
Do not route an L9 presupposition and this cap through the same item
01a0c6d5 looked like this mode (runs set above a co-solvent's boiling point) but used sealed reactors, where that is routine: a limit that holds for one vessel type is T9 territory, not R2
kills: a stated capacity figure (slots per week, person-days available)
a field or question asking whether the plan is feasible
a remark that the target was set before the rota or timetable was known
trace_signals: the user says the plan is impossible for the people or equipment available
targets derived from conversion ratios or desired outputs with no supply-side check
the assistant concedes it set figures before knowing the capacity
modes.example: A clinic manager's KPI sheet derives monthly new-patient evaluations from lead volume and conversion rates. The dentist's rota holds evaluation sessions on two afternoons, one of them in alternate weeks only; the receptionist's handbook says each evaluation fills one session slot of a stated length. Deliverable: next month's weekly evaluation bookings, leads to contact and expected attendances.

traces.signal: Assistant derived monthly evaluation targets from conversion rates; user said one professional cannot see that many patients.
One-year fieldwork plan with repeated country visits; user asked how teaching lecturers could manage it; assistant conceded.
